course_description:
This course critically examines the relationship between culture, identity and communication.

In an increasingly interconnected world,ﾠthe ability to understand who, what, when, where, why and how to communicate effectively and appropriatelyﾠacrossﾠcultures isﾠessential at individual, group, community, organisational, national, and international levels. This courseﾠintroduces theories and skills of research and professional practices in intercultural communication. Students will critically reviewﾠtheories and applyﾠtheories to resolve practical problems emerging from everyday communication in diverse cultural contexts. The goal of this course is to equip students with the capacity of autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability, and responsibility as an effective intercultural communicator in the global society.

course_aims:
This course aims to examine the interrelationships between communication and culture. It builds your knowledge of howﾠculture influencesﾠattitudesﾠand communication behaviours including perception, stereotypes, conflict management, human relationships, media, communication technologies, as well as exploresﾠthe dynamics of the global and the local cultures. In doing so, the course equips you with the capacity to communicate effectively and appropriately with people in diverse cultural contexts.

This course believes that becoming competent intercultural communicators requiresﾠthe abilityﾠto critically examine one's own cultural assumptions and how those assumptions influence their communication behaviours. An awareness of how communication and culture mutually influence each other generates insights into people's particular ways of thinking, doing, and being, which in turn, influences intercultural communication.ﾠCritical thinking and reflectionﾠare emphasised throughﾠall learning activities and assessments to encourageﾠstudents to make connections between the theoretical concepts learnedﾠin the course and their own practicalﾠexperiences.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognise the influence of culture on communication between individuals, groups, organisations, and nations.
Critically reflect on the influence of culture on how you view your own cultural group and cultural groups other than your own.
Effectively apply verbal and non-verbal communication knowledge and skills in intercultural communication contexts.
Effectively apply theories and concepts in analysing intercultural communication problems and provide solutions.
Demonstrate respect, expert judgment, adaptability, and responsibility as an effective and ethical communicator in diverse cultural contexts.

assessment_details.title: Reflective Essay
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment requires you to examine and reflect on your own culture as an insider. This assessment is not simply a general description of your culture. Your reflective essay should begin with your cultural identification to convey who you are as a member of the cultural group with which you identify. You are required then to explain what beliefs, values, practices, traditions and so forth are important to you as a member of your cultural group, and why they are important to you. Your cultural group can be defined at the national level (e.g., Australia, Germany, Japan) or at sub-cultural levels (e.g., ethnicity, religion, geographic region). You need to apply theories and concepts of communication and culture learned in the course. You may also search in the literature for other relevant theories beyond what is covered in the course and apply them in your reflective essay where appropriate. You must define all key concepts which you have included in your reflective essay and demonstrate your ability to apply them in appropriate contexts. Your reflection explains how your culture shapes your thinking (attitudes), doing (behaviours), and being (cultural identity). You are required to cite at least 3 academic references from academic journals or books. Include all references cited within your reflective essay in the references list at the end of your reflective essay. APA 7th edition referencing style is required. The UQ Library website has APA 7th edition referencing style guide. I nclude the following sections in your reflective essay: Title of your reflective essay. Brief description of the culture with which you identify and the aspects of culture that you choose to focus on (e.g., values, beliefs, traditions, or customs, etc.). Definition of key concepts that your reflective essay used, explanation of how they are applied in your essay, and justification for why they are important to you as a member of the cultural group with which you identify. Your reflection on how your culture shapes your thinking, doing, and being. References list with all references cited within your reflective essay (in-text citation) arranged according to APA 7th edition referencing style guide. Note: This assessment should be submitted via Turnitin. Submission as email attachment will NOT be accepted. The word limit (1500 words) is suggestive. No penalties will be applied to your assessment based on the sole reason that it is over or under the suggested word limit. Your assessment is graded based on the marking criteria provided. It is NOT graded with reference to the achievement of other students in the course or your performance in other courses. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: In-Class Tests (5 tests)
assessment_details.task_description: Assessment 2 consists of 5 in-class tests to be conducted in person during tutorial sessions of 5 weeks, starting in Week 5 and ending in Week 9 (inclusive). The duration of each test is about 30 minutes. The in-class tests are identity verified, in person and closed-book tests. Electronic devices, learning materials, readings, and written notes are not permitted during each test. Tutors will provide hard copies of test worksheets to students in the tutorial session of the week in which a test is scheduled. Students submit their completed test worksheets to their tutor at the end of the test time in the tutorial session. In-class tests are in the format of short-answer questions. The question(s) of each test are based on the learning resources of a specific week including lecture notes and power points, tutorial notes and power points, lecture, tutorial, and required readings. More details of in-class tests will be provided in class sessions and on Blackboard. Note: Each completed in-class test worksheet is to be submitted in the tutorial session in which the test is conducted. Submission of a completed in-class test worksheet to the course coordinator or tutor as email attachment will NOT be accepted. Your assessment is graded based on the marking criteria specified in this course, NOT graded with reference to the achievement of other students or your performance in other courses. assessment_details.title: Case Studies
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment requires you to apply theories learned in the course and/or other relevant theories that you have searched in the literature to analyse cases in which intercultural communication problems occurred. You need to choose two cases from the list of case studies provided in the Assessment 3 folder on Blackboard course site. You need to analyse the two cases you have chosen to identify the intercultural problems in each case and then provide specific solutions. You should apply theories of intercultural communication learned in the course and/or other relevant theories you have searched in the literature in analysing problems and providing specific solutions to the identified problems. You are required to reflect on your learning about intercultural communication through your analysis of the intercultural communication cases. You need to cite at least 5 academic references from academic books or journals. Include all references cited within your essay in a references list at the end of your assessment. APA 7th edition referencing style is required. The UQ Library website has APA 7th edition referencing style guide. Include the following sections in your assessment: Title: Provide a specific title for your essay of case studies. Introduction: State briefly the cases that you have chosen and provide a justification for why you have chosen those two cases for your assessment. Analyse the intercultural communication problems in the two case studies you have chosen and provide specific solutions by drawing on theories learned in the course and/or other relevant theories that you have searched in the literature. This demonstrates your knowledge and ability to apply knowledge in appropriate contexts. Reflection: Reflect on what you have learned about intercultural communication from analysing the two cases studies you have chosen. References: All references cited within the essay must be included in the references list that is arranged according to APA 7th edition referencing style guide. Note: This assessment should be submitted via Turnitin. Submission as email attachment will NOT be accepted. The word limit (2000 words) is suggestive. No penalties will be applied to your assessment based on the sole reason that it is over or under the suggested word limit. Your assessment is graded based on the marking criteria published in the ECP. learning_activities.topic: Week 1 Lecture: Introduction to the Course The first lecture provides an overview of the course, including aims and learning outcomes, learning resources, assessment summary, and course requirements. Learning outcomes: L01
Week 1 Tutorial: No tutorials No tutorials in Week 1. Tutorials start in Week 2.

Week 2 Lecture: Communication and Culture This lecture discusses components and characteristics of culture as well as explores the relationships between communication and culture. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 2 Tutorial: The Influence of Culture on Communication This tutorial examines various ways in which culture and communication mutually influence each other. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 3 Lecture: Self-Directed Learning NO LECTURE Self-Directed Learning. There is no lecture this week due to EKKA Public Holiday on 12/08/2026.
Week 3 Tutorial: Self-Directed Learning NO TUTORIAL Self-directed learning. There are no tutorials this week due to EKKA Public Holiday on 12/08/2026.

Week 4 Lecture: Perception and Categorisation This lecture explores the process of perception and social categorisation as well as the influence of culture on perception and social categorisation. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05
Week 4 Tutorial: Social categorisation and Intergroup Relations This tutorial analyses the influence of culture on social categorisation and intergroup relations. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

Week 5 Lecture: Cultural Dimensions and Behaviours This lecture discusses the relationship between orientations to cultural dimensions and behaviours. It also introduces ethical principles governing intercultural communication. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 5 Tutorial: Culture and Intergroup Communication This tutorial applies cultural dimensions to analyse attitudes and behaviours in intergroup communication. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 6 Lecture: Verbal and Nonverbal Communication This lecture examines characteristics of verbal and nonverbal codes as well as discusses the influence of culture on communication styles. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 6 Tutorial: Language and Culture This tutorial analyses ways in which culture influences the use of verbal and nonverbal codes in diverse cultural contexts. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 7 Lecture: Cultural Diversity and Acculturation This lecture discusses immigration, acculturation, and factors influencing cross-cultural adaptation outcomes. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 7 Tutorial: Immigration and Accultuation This tutorial explores acculturation strategies, processes and outcomes. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 8 Lecture: Identities and Human Relationships This lecture explores identities, identity negotiation and human relationship development. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 8 Tutorial: Human Relationships and Culture This tutorial applies cultural identity theories to analyse the influence of culture on human relationship development. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 9 Lecture: Media and Cultural Change This lecture discusses the role of media and communication technologies in bringing about cultural change in society. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 9 Tutorial: Media, Communication Technologies and Culture This tutorial analyses how media including digital media influence cultural change in society. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Mid-Semester Break This week is Mid-Semester Break. No lecture and no tutorials. Enjoy your Mid-Semester Break!
Week 10 Lecture: Self-Directed Learning NO LECTURE Self-Directed Learning. There is no lecture this week due to King's Birthday Public Holiday on 05/10/2026.
Week 10 Tutorial: Self-Directed Learning NO TUTORIAL Self-Directed Learning. There are no tutorials this week due to King's Birthday Public Holiday on 05/10/2026.
Week 11 Lecture: Diversity and Conflict Management This lecture introduces conflict management strategies and diversity management in workplaces. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 11 Tutorial: Working with People of Diverse Cultures This tutorial explores diversity and management of diversity in workplaces. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 12 Lecture: Intercultural Communication in Families This lecture examines strategies of intercultural communication in family contexts and discusses identity negotiation of third culture individuals. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 12 Tutorial: Intergenerational Communication in Families This tutorial explores intergenerational communication in family contexts. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 13 Lecture: Intercultural Communication Competence This final lecture of the course discusses components of intercultural communication competence and building intercultural communication competence. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 13 Tutorial: Q&A Drop-In Session This final tutorial of the course is a drop-in Q&A session. If you don't have any questions about the course, you don't need to attend the tutorial.
